Indicates the transaction type associated with the row.

Indicates the batch ID associated with the batch. Use the value for this attribute from the Manage Item Batches page. Indicates the batch number associated with the batch. Use the value for this attribute from the Manage Item Batches page. You should use batch ID instead of this attribute. The batch number attribute will be deprecated in a future release
Unique number associated with the item.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the item can be added to an outside processing purchase order. If N, then the item can't be added to an outside processing purchase order.
Code that identifies the organization. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Inventory Organizations task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Description of the part, item, product, or service.

Name of the template to apply to the item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Item Classes task. The default template is set at the item class.
Defines the Source System Code. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Source System task in the Setup and Maintenance work area. Identifies whether the batch is PIM or Non PIM batch.
Defines the Source System Item Reference. This indicates the unique identifier of the item in the external source system.
Defines the Source System Item Description. This indicates the desription of the item in the external source system.
Value that uniquely identifies the item class. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Item Classes task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Primary unit of measure of the item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Units of Measures task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Name of lifecycle phase of the item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Lifecycle Phases task.
Status of the transaction activity for the item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Item Statuses task.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then item is classified as an asset item. If N, then item isn't classified as an asset item.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then maintainable assets can be defined for the item. If N, then maintainable assets can't be defined for the item.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the item is enabled for genealogy tracking. If N, then the item isn't enabled for genealogy tracking.

Value that identifies the asset class of the item. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_CSE_ASSET_CLASS. Review and update the value for this attribute using and the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then item costs are reported and accounted. If N, then item costs are not reported and accounted.

Amount of a particular item that is ordered from the plant or a supplier, or issued as a standard quantity to the production process. Oracle Cost Management Cloud uses this value to calculate unit costs for sub-elements with a lot basis type.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then item is valued as an asset in inventory. If N, then item isn't valued as an asset in inventory.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then item is included in the cost rollup. If N, then item isn't included in the cost rollup.
Fixed costs that are associated with placing a sales order for the item.
Minimum days of supply to allow before replenishing the item.
Fixed quantity to reorder in the inventory that the vendor manages.
Minimum quantity for the sales order or repetitive rate in the number of units for each day.
Contains one of the following values: 1 or 2. If 1, then automatically expire the advance shipment notice. If 2, then don't automatically expire the advance shipment notice.
Percent of unit cost that represents the internal cost to stock one unit for one year.
Contains one of the following values: 1 or 2. If 1, then the item resides at your location but the supplier owns it. If 2, then the item resides at your location and you own it.
Number of days to modify the size and timing of each planned order quantity.
Multiplier to use, in units for each day, for each fixed lot quantity or each repetitive rate.
Quantity to use to modify the size of each planned order quantity or each repetitive daily rate.
Time period to use when forecasting demand for the item.

Value that indicates the type of planning that will be used for the item. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_MATERIAL_PLANNING . Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Value that identifies the method to use when planning the safety stock for the item.
Number of days to use when calculating the average daily demand.
Number of days of cover for the item. The application multiplies Days of Cover by the average demand to calculate the safety stock level.
Minimum order quantity of the item.
Maximum order quantity or repetitive rate in units for each day.
Value indicates the material planner for the item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Material Planners task.

Value that identifies whether your organization manufactures or buys the item. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_PLANNING_MAKE_BUY. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Organization that owns the source subinventory. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Inventory Organizations task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.

Value that identifies how to replenish inventory that the requests have depleted. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_SOURCE_TYPES. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.

Value that uniquely identifies the type of authorization required before creating the sales order. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_MSI_GP_RELEASE_AUTH. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.

Value that indicates the subcontracting type associated to this item when it is used as a subcontracting component in chargeable subcontracting. Values include Prepositioned and Synchronized. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_SUBCONT_COMPONENT. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.

Value that uniquely identifies the type of demand for the item. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_ATO_FORECAST_CONTROL. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Value that indicates the maximum order to replenish the item.
Maximum days of supply to allow before replenishing the item.
Organization that an internal requisition uses as the source to get the item.

Contains one of the following values:1 or 2. If 1, then restrict the transactions of the item from the subinventory. If 2, then don't restrict the transactions of the item from the subinventory. The default value is true.
Contains one of the following values: 1 or 2. If 1, then restrict the transactions of the item from the locator. If 2, then don't restrict the transactions of the item from the locator.

Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then if parent lot is specified, use lot control on the item during the transaction. If N, then don't use lot control on the item during the transaction.
Alphabetic prefix to add to the child lot.
First number to use in a sequence of numbers for the child lot.

Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then make sure the child lot numbers conform to the child lot parameters. If N, then don't make sure the child lot numbers conform to the child lot parameters.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the child lot inherits the parent lot attributes. If N, then the child lot doesn't inherit the parent lot attributes.
Internal value that indicates the default action to be taken for this item when the lot expires or the lot fails a quality check.
Number of days the application adds to the expiration date before taking an action on the lot.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the item can be stocked in inventory. If N, then the item can't be stocked in inventory.
Starting number associated with the lot numbers when they are automatically created for an item.

Value that indicates how long items in a given lot remain available. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_SHELF_LIFE_CODE_TYPE. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Number of days that each lot is active.

Value that indicates the number assigned to each unit of an item and is used to track the item. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_SERIAL_NUMBER_CONTROL_TYPE. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then transactions on the item is restricted to the subinventory. If N, then transactions on the item isn't restricted to the subinventory.

Contains one of the following values: 1 or 2. If 2, then the item is under revision control and it includes inventory attributes. If 1, then the item isn't under revision control and it includes inventory attributes.
Number of days after the creation date before retesting the lot.
Prefix associated when lot numbers are automatically created for an item.
Prefix associated when serial numbers are automatically created for an item.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then pick items in bulk. If N, then don't pick items in bulk.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then check for material shortages for the item. If N, then don't check for material shortages for the item.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the item is scheduled for automatic cycle count. If N, then the item isn't cycle counted.
Value that indicates default grade for the item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Lot Grades task.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the item is grade controlled in addition to lot controlled. If N, then the item isn't grade controlled.
Number of days to add to the lot creation date that determines when you can release the lot.

Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then allow the application to allocate, reserve, or move partial lot quantities. If N, then don't allow the application to allocate, reserve, or move partial lot quantities.
Number of days to add to the lot creation date to determine the lot maturity date.
Internal value that indicates the default lot status for the item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Material Statuses task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Internal value that indicates the default serial status of the item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Material Statuses task
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the lot-controlled item can be split into many lots. If N, then the lot-controlled item can't be split into many lots.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then allow the application to merge multiple lots into one lot for an item that lots control. If N, then don't allow this merge.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the item can be stocked and transacted. If N, then the item can't be stocked and transacted.

Value that indicates the physical area within a subinventory where you store material, such as a row, aisle, bin, or shelf. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_LOCATOR_CONTROL_CODE_TYPE. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area

Value that indicates the ability to use lot numbers during material transactions for tracking of batches of Item. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_LOT_CONTROL_CODE_TYPE. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then item lot is status controlled at the lot level. If N, then item lot isn't status controlled.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then allow the application to substitute a lot in the transaction. If N, then don't allow this substitution.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then Item lots can be translated. If N, then Item Lots can't be translated.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then transactions can be performed on the item. If N, then transactions can't be performed on the item.
Maximum positive difference to allow between the cycle count quantity and the on-hand quantity that the application monitors.
Maximum negative difference to allow between the cycle count quantity and the on-hand quantity that the application monitors.

Value that uniquely identifies how to create child lot numbers for the item. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_PARENT_CHILD_GEN_TYPE. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Contains one of the following values: 1 or 2. If 1, then create material reservations for the item. If 2, then don't create material reservations for the item.
Starting number associated with the serial numbers when they are automatically created for an item

Value that indicates invoicing rule to determine the period in which an invoice is sent. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Manage Invoicing Rules task in the the Setup and Maintenance work area.

Value that indicates a tax code to use when calculating tax based on location and tax codes. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Tax Codes task.
Account used when tracking a sales item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Keyflex Fields task.
Internal value that indicates a valid payment terms code. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Payment Terms task.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then item can be invoiced in Oracle Receivables Cloud. If N, then item can't be invoiced.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then item can be invoiced at this point of time in Oracle Receivables Cloud. If N, then item can't be invoiced at this point of time.

Value that indicates the accounting rule to identify special revenue recognition rules for an item. Review and update the value for this attribute using the Setup and Maintenance work area, and the Manage Accounting Rules task.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then item is created automatically. If N, then item isn't created automatically.

Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, the item is generally built for sales order demand and a final assembly work order is created based on sales order details. If N, then assembly work order isn't created for the item.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then items can be picked from finished goods inventory. If N, then items can't be picked from finished goods inventory.
Value that uniquely identifies the model to use when creating an assemble-to-order configuration.

Value that indicates how to calculate lead time based on Date, Model, or Unit Number. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_BOM_EFFEC_CTRL. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.

Value that indicates whether the configured bill of materials can be created based on item or sourcing. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_CONFIG_ORG. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.

Value that indicates the capability to match to one of existing configurations of the models. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_CONFIG_MATCH. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.

Value that indicates the behavior of the configurable models in the configurator. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_CONFIG_MODEL. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.

Value that indicates the type of bill of material the item can possess. Values include standard, model, planning, and other. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_BOM_ITEM_TYPE. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area.
Number of days required to manufacture the item, including the adjusted, cumulative, and total lead time for the component that requires the longest time to assemble.
Value that indicates the days that must be added to the purchasing or manufacturing lead time to place an order.
Number of days required to assemble the item, including the adjusted, cumulative, and total lead time for the component that requires the longest time to assemble.
Number of days required to assemble an item independent of the sales order quantity, such as setup time or teardown time.
Time to produce one unit of an assembly.
Number of days required to procure or manufacture the item.
Quantity to use when computing the processing lead time.
Number of days required to receive a purchased item into inventory from the supplier receipt.

Value that uniquely identifies the type of forecast demand to use for the item. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_ATO_FORECAST_CONTROL. Review the value for this attribute using the Manage Standard Lookups task in the Setup and Maintenance work area
Contains one of the following values:1 or 2. If 1, then it indicates Yes. If 2, it indicates No.
Number of days before which the planning process won't reschedule the sales order.
Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then suggest supply for this item. If N, then don't suggest supply for this item.
Days of supply in the target inventory that the planning process must create to achieve the desired business metric, such as throughput rate, cost, due date performance, inventory and days of supply.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies each asset row for the selected Batch Code. It is recommended to create unique values for the interface record number for each asset row. This will help with tracking and error resolution during the upload and import processes.
Abbreviation that specifies if the asset should be Created or Updated. Valid values are CREATE and UPDATE as defined in lookup ORA_CSE_ASSET_IMPORT_ACTION.

Number that uniquely identifies the asset. Your spreadsheet can’t have duplicate assets During CREATE, the value optional. If a number is defined, the value can be alphanumeric and must be unique for each asset in this worksheet and not already exist in the asset table. If the number is set = null, then the system will generate a sequential number. During UPDATE, an asset number value is required.

Number that uniquely identifies the new asset number for an existing asset. During CREATE, value should be set = null. During UPDATE, the value is optional. The new asset number is only required if you wish to change the number of an existing asset, else set the value = null.

The description of the asset. Used to describe the features, characteristics, and aspects of the asset. The description is optional to CREATE or UPDATE of an asset. During CREATE, if set = Null, then the description defaults from the description of the asset's associated Item Number. During UPDATE, the value is optional. A value should only be passed if you wish to change the description, else set the value = null.

An indicator that specifies whether an asset hierarchy should be created based on the Item Number's bill of materials. During CREATE, if the Flag is set = Y, then child assets will be created under the parent asset. Valid values Y or N. The default value is N if not defined. During UPDATE, the value should be set = null.

An indicator that specifies whether an asset should synchronized with the IoT Cloud Asset Monitoring Service during CREATE or UPDATE actions. During CREATE, if the Flag is set = Y, then a digital twin will be created in IOT, if the service is enabled. Valid values Y or N. The default value is Y if not defined, regardless if the IoT Service is enabled or not. During UPDATE, if the Flag is already set = Y, then key asset attributes will be updated in the digital twin. An indicator that specifies whether an Item Number is required for an asset during the CREATE action. During CREATE, if set = Y, then an Item Number is required. If set = N, then an Item Number is not required, allowing for the creation of a description-based asset. Valid values Y or N. The default value is Y if not defined. During UPDATE, the value should be set = null.
An indicator that specifies whether an asset is a competitor asset. During CREATE or UPDATE, the Flag is optional. Valid values Y or N. The default value is N if not defined.

Abbreviation for the organization where the asset is created or is expected to be operated and maintained. Number of the inventory item for which the asset is based. During CREATE, the value is required if the Item Required Flag = Y. Else, it is not required. For a maintainable asset, the item number must be full life cycle tracked and the Organization Code must be enabled for the item. For a non-maintainable asset, the item number must be defined as customer tracked. During UPDATE, the value should be set = null.

Quantity of product that the asset references. During CREATE, a value is required. If a Serial Number is defined, then the quantity cannot exceed a value of one. Else, for a Lot Controlled asset, the value can be = one or greater. During UPDATE, the value should be set = null.

If the Item Number Required Flag = N, then a valid Code is required. During UPDATE, the value should be set = null if the Asset is based on an Item Number. For

Secondary quantity of product that the asset references. Values should only be defined if the Item Number Required Flag = Y and the Item Number is enabled for Dual UOM. During CREATE, if the Item Number Defaulting Control is set to Not Default, a value is required. If set to Default, then a value is optional. If set to Fixed, then no value should be defined. Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the asset secondary quantity UOM. Values should only be defined if the Item Number Required Flag = Y and the Item Number is enabled for Dual UOM. During CREATE, a value is optional. If defined, the value must be the same as the Item Number's secondary UOM. If not defined, then the value is defaulted from the Item Number's secondary UOM. During UPDATE, the value may be updated to a valid value from the Item Number. Else, the value should be set = null.

Number that uniquely identifies the asset, usually from the manufacturer. During CREATE, the serial number is optional and can only be defined if the Item Number is defined as serial controlled. Number that uniquely identifies the asset based on the item inventory lot. During CREATE, the Lot Number is optional and can only be defined if the Item Number is defined as enabled for Lot Control. If a value is passed for a non-lot controlled Item Number, the value is ignored. During UPDATE, a value should be defined only if the lot number has changed, else the value should be set = null.

Date when the asset becomes inactive. The Asset End Date is optional to CREATE or UPDATE an asset. During CREATE, if a value is defined, then the Date must be in the future and must be after the Customer Asset End Date, if defined. During UPDATE, if a value is defined, then the Date must be in the past, present or future, but must be after the Customer Asset End Date, if defined. In general, Asset attributes can only be revised until a value is defined for this Date.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the location context where the asset currently resides. During CREATE, the Code is required. The Code values include: Customer Address, External Address, Internal Address, Work Center, and Unknown. If set = Null, then the value will defaulted to Unknown. The list of values is defined in lookup ORA_CSE_CURRENT_LOC_CONTEXT. During UPDATE, a Code is only required if the Location Type has changed for the asset, else set = null.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the organization where the asset is located. During CREATE, the Code is required when the Location Type Code = Work Center, else set = null. During UPDATE, a Code is only required if the Location Type has changed for the asset and the Location Type = Work Center, else set = null.

Abbreviation that identifies the work center where the asset is located. During CREATE, the Code is required when the Location Type Code = Work Center, else set = null. During UPDATE, the Code is only required if Work Center has changed, else set = null

Second line of the external address where the asset is located. During CREATE, the Address2 is optional when the Location Type Code = External Address, else set = null. The address fields will be used to find a matching External Party location code.

Country where the asset is located. During CREATE, the Country is required when the Location Type Code = External Address, else set = null. The address fields will be used to find a matching External Party location code.

Abbreviation that identifies the postal area where the asset resides. During CREATE, the Postal Code is required when the Location Type Code = External Address, else set = null. The address fields will be used to find a matching External Party location code.

County where the asset is located. During CREATE, the County is required when the Location Type Code = External Address, else set = null. The address fields will be used to find a matching External Party location code.

Value that identifies the sales order that was used to order the asset. During CREATE, this value is optional for a Customer Asset. During UPDATE, a number is only required if the Sales Order reference has changed for the asset, else set = null.

Date and time when the customer purchased the asset. During CREATE, this value is required for a Customer Asset if the Registration Date is defined and the value must be before the Registration Date. Else the Date is optional or should be set = null. During UPDATE, if the Registration Date is defined, then the value must be before the Registration Date. Date when the application ships the asset to the customer. During CREATE, the Date is required for a Customer Asset. The Date may be set to a past, present or future date. If set = Null, then for a Customer Asset the date is defaulted to the system current date. During UPDATE, the Date may be set to a past, present or future date.

Date and time when the organization installed the asset. During CREATE, this value is optional for a Customer Asset. If defined, then the Date must be greater than the Shipment Date and less than the In Service Date, else set = null. During UPDATE the Date the Date must be greater than the Shipment Date and less than the In Service Date, else it should be set = null.

Date and time when the organization put the asset in service. During CREATE, this value is optional for a Customer Asset. If defined, then the Date must be greater than the Installed Date, else set= null. During UPDATE the Date the Date must be greater than the Installed Date, else it should be set = null.

Date and time when the customer registered the asset. During CREATE, this value is optional for a Customer Asset. If defined, the Purchase Date is required. Else the Date should be set = null. During UPDATE, if the Registration Date has changed, then the value must be greater than the Customer Purchase Date, else it should be set = null.

Date and time that represents the completion of an asset’s lifecycle with a customer or at a customer's site. During CREATE or UPDATE, this value is optional for a Customer Asset. If defined, the value can be not be set to a future date and must be after the Shipment Date. Additionally, it must be less than the Asset End Date. Else set this value = null. Once defined, you cannot update other asset attributes. During UPDATE, to remove the End Date value, pass a value = #NULL.

Abbreviation that identifies the pricing element of the pricing charge. This attribute is required to define the charge for asset pricing.
Abbreviation that indicates whether the unit price in the pricing element is the list price or the net price.
Contains one of the following values. Y: the asset price includes taxes. N: the asset price does not include taxes. The default value is N.

User defined import reference for a unique header record for a maintenance work order within a Batch Code. During CREATE and UPDATE a unique Header Number value is required for each Work Order. The Header Number is also used as a reference to the unique Work Order in each detail tab, supporting the CREATE and UPDATE actions for work order details.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the import action to be performed on the work order header and detail tabs. A value is always required to CREATE or UPDATE the Work Order header or its detail tabs. If set = CREATE, then the Work Order Header details in this tab must be defined. Optionally, data in the detail tabs can be created at the same time. if set = UPDATE, then the Work Order Header details in this tab can be optionally updated. Additionally, the data in the other tabs can be created

Number that uniquely identifies the work order in a maintenance organization. During CREATE, you can manually define a unique Work Order Number. Else set = Null and the system will automatically create a unique sequential number following the definitions in the Organizations Plant Parameters: Work Order Prefix and Work Order Starting Number. During UPDATE, the Work Order Number is required to provide reference for the update of the Work Order header and detail tabs.
Abbreviation that identifies the maintenance Organization in which the work order is executed. During CREATE and UPDATE, the Organization Code is required.

Number that uniquely identifies the item that the work order asset references. Item number is required for creating multiple asset maintenance work orders. When the value for "AllowMultipleAssetsFlag" is true then it is a required field. When the value for "AllowMultipleAssetsFlag" is false then it is derived from work order asset reference value.

Number that uniquely identifies the item that the work order asset could reference after the compeltion of the work order. If the work order has a value for target item attribute, then the work order is called transform work order. Asset transformation is allowed conditionally for all kinds of maintenance work orders except for work orders with non serial asset.

Planned maintenance work order quantity. When the value for AllowMultipleAssetsFlag is false, it's a single asset maintenance work order and the value is derived from the asset quantity. When the value for AllowMultipleAssetsFlag is true, then the multiple asset work order and value is required at the time of work order creation along with item information.

An indicator that specifies whether the work order support single or multiple assets.Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the work order can be associated with more than one asset. If N, then the work order can be associated with only one asset. The default value is N. This value cannot be updated in the work order.

An indicator that specifies whether the work order completes the asset to inventory. Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the work order completes the work order assets to inventory. If N, then the work order does not complete the work order assets to inventory. The default value is N. This value can be updated when the work order is in unreleased status
Allow Out of Sequence Operation Completion Flag

An indicator that specifies whether the work order operations are completed in sequence or otherwise.Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the work order operations can be completed out of sequence. If N, then the work order operations are completed in sequence. The default value is N. This value can be updated when the work order is in an unreleased status

An indicator that specifies whether the work order is considered for inventory planning purposes and applicable for inventory completion work ordes. Contains one of the following values: Y or N. If Y, then the work order will be considered for inventory planning especially MIN/ MAX planning. The value can be Y only when the "Allow Completion to Inventory Flag is Y. If N, then the work order wii not be considered for inventory planning purposes. The default value is N. This value can be updated w

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the Status of an order. Valid values are defined in lookup ORA_WIE_WO_SYSTEM_STATUS. During CREATE, the Status Code is optional. If a Work Definition Code is defined, then the Status Code can be set to ORA_UNRELEASED, ORA_RELEASED or ORA_HOLD. If a Work Definition is not defined, then the Status can only be set to ORA_UNRELEASED, ORA_HOLD. If set = Null, then the status is set to ORA_UNRELEASED. During UPDATE, you can optionally pass a new Status, else set =

Date when the work order is planned to Start. During CREATE, you must provide either the Planned Start Date or the Planned Completion Date. Date format is YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS. If MM/DD/YYYY or Day-Month is entered, It will be converted into the correct date and time format within the cell. If not defined, then the default value is the system date. During UPDATE, you can pass an updated Start Date, else set = Null,

Date when the work order is planned to Complete. During CREATE, you must provide either the Planned Start Date or the Planned Completion Date. Date format is YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS. If MM/DD/YYYY or Day-Month is entered, It will be converted into the correct date and time format within the cell. If not defined, then the default value is the system date. During UPDATE, you can pass an updated Completion Date, else set = Null,

The description of the maintenance work order. During CREATE, the Description is optional. If a Work Definition Code is defined, then the Description is defaulted from the Work Definition description. During UPDATE, the Description can be updated, else Set = null.

The long description of the maintenance work order. During CREATE, the Description is optional. If a Work Definition Code is defined, then the Description is defaulted from the Work Definition long description. During UPDATE, the Description can be updated, else Set = null.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the Type of a work order. Valid values are CORRECTIVE or PREVENTIVE. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type ORA_MNT_WO_TYPE. During CREATE, the Type is required. If not defined, then the Type will default from the Asset or Work Definition. During UPDATE, the Type can only be updated before the Work Order is Released, else set = null.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the Subtype of a work order. The list of accepted values is defined in user extensible lookup type ORA_MNT_WO_SUB_TYPE. During CREATE, the Subtype is required. If not defined, then the Subtype will default from the Asset or Work Definition. During UPDATE, the Subtype can only be updated before the Work Order is Released, else set = null.
Number that indicates the priority of the work order. During CREATE and UPDATE, the Priority is optional.

Indicator that determines if Supply Planning engine collects the work order for scheduling or rescheduling using the Scheduling Method. Valid values are Y or N. The default value is N if not defined. During Create or Update, a value can be defined, else set = null. If set = Y, then the Scheduling Method will not be used. If set = N, then the Scheduling Method will be used.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the Maintenance Work Definition used as the basis for the work order. During CREATE, the Definition is optional. If defined, then it is used for to create each operation and its resource and material details. If not defined, then operations and details must be manually defined. During UPDATE, the Definition can only be updated before the Work Order is Released. If updated, then all the work order operations details are replaced by the new Definition. Else se

Date as of which the work definiton should be active. Allows for previous versions of a Work Definition to be used based on the defined date. During CREATE, if a Work Definition is defined, then the Date is optional. If set = null, then the Date is set to the present date. Date format is YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS. If MM/DD/YYYY or Day-Month is entered, It will be converted into the correct date and time format within the cell. During UPDATE, if the Work Definition is updated, then a Date can be option

An indicator that specifies whether the work order is exploded or re-exploded based on the Work Definition code, if defined. The valid values Y or N. The default value is Y if not defined. During CREATE, if a Work Definition is defined, then the Flag is optional. If set = Y, then the work order is exploded or re-exploded based on the work definition code. This will create all the operations, materials and resources. If set = N. then the work order is not created based on the work definition. The

Method for Work Order Scheduling. During CREATE or UPDATE, the Method is required and will determine if the work order needs to be scheduled, re-scheduled or not scheduled. If set = Default Scheduler, then Planning engine will schedule the work order, operation and resource dates. If set = No Scheduling, then you must pass work order, operation and resource dates manually. Updates to these dates flow top-down. Valid values are DEFAULT_SCHEDULER and NO_SCHEDULING.
Source system header level reference for the work order. During CREATE or UPDATE, the Reference is optional.
Source system line level reference for the work order. During CREATE or UPDATE, the Reference Line is optional.
Source system header reference identifier. During CREATE or UPDATE, the Reference ID is optional.
Source system line reference identifier. During CREATE or UPDATE, the Reference Line ID is optional.

Value that indicates the reason for which a work order status is set to Canceled. During CREATE, a work order can't be cancelled, so the Reaon is ignored, set = Null During UPDATE, if a work order is set to a status = Cancelled, then the Reason is required and can be defined or updated.

Date when the work order actually starts. During CREATE, you can only pass a date if the status is not Unreleased, else set= Null. During UPDATE, the value of this attribute is set when the first transaction is performed against a Released work order Date format is YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS. Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the import action to be performed on the work order operations for a unique header. Valid values are CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE from the lookup ORA_WIE_WO_IMP_DETAIL_ACTION. During CREATE, if a Work Definition code is defined on the Work Orders tab, then do not pass any Operation rows. If a Work Definition is not defined, then you can CREATE individual operations for each work order header. During UPDATE, you can CREATE new Operation Sequence rows in a work orde

Unique header record of a Maintenance Work Order within a Batch Code. During CREATE and UPDATE a unique Header Number value is required. The Header Number is used as a reference to the work order in each detail tab, supporting the CREATE and UPDATE actions for work order details.

Value of the Sequence used when performing the work order operations. The Sequence value must be a positive integer and be unique within the work order header. During CREATE, if a Work Definition is not defined, then a unique operation sequence is required to CREATE each operation within a work order header. If set = null, then the Sequence will be automatically set to a value calculated by incrementing the last operation Sequence by a value of 10. Additionally, new Operation Sequences can be CR

Abbreviation for the Standard Operation that can be optionally used to create a Operation Sequence in a work order header. During CREATE, the Code is optional. If defined, then the Operation Sequence will be defined using an Standard Operation. If not defined, then the Operation Sequence must be manually defined and the Operation Type and Name are required. During UPDATE, the Code can't be updated, so set = null. However, its Name and Description can be updated.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the Type of Operation Sequence in a work order header. Valid values include IN_HOUSE or SUPPLIER. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type ORA_WIS_OPERATION_TYPE. During CREATE, the Type is required. If a Standard Operation Code is defined, then set = Null. If a Standard Operation Code isn't defined, then a Type is required. If not passed, then the default value is IN_HOUSE. During UPDATE, the Type can't be updated, so set = null.

Name of the Operation Sequence in a work order header. During CREATE, the Name is required if a Standard Operation Code is not passed, else set = null. During UPDATE, an existing Name can be updated for a Standard or Manually defined Operation Sequence, else set = null.

Description of the Operation Sequence in a work order header. During CREATE, the Description is optional if a Standard Operation Code is not passed, else set = null. During UPDATE, an existing Description can be updated for a Standard or Manually defined Operation Sequence, else set = null.

Long Description of the Operation Sequence in a work order. During CREATE, the Long Description is optional if a Standard Operation Code is not passed, if passed the standard Operation long description is carried over to work order operation. During UPDATE, an existing Description can be updated for a Standard or Manually defined Operation Sequence, else set = null.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the Work Center in which the Operation Sequence is performed. During CREATE, the Work Center Code is required if a Standard Operation Code is not passed, else set = null. During UPDATE, an existing Work Center code can be updated, only if an Operation Sequence was not created from a Standard Operation. Else set = null.

Date when the Operation Sequence is planned to start. The scheduling application sets this date. During CREATE or UPDATE, the Date is required. If set = null, then it is defaulted to the work order planned start date. If manually defined, the Scheduled Start Date must not occur before the start date of the work order or after the finish date of the work order. Date format is YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS. If MM/DD/YYYY or Day-Month is entered, It will be converted into the correct date and time format wit

Date when the Operation Sequence is planned to finish. The scheduling application sets this date. During CREATE or UPDATE, the Date is required. If set = null, then it is defaulted to the work order planned completion date. If manually defined, the Scheduled End Date must not occur before the start date of the work order or after the finish date of the work order. Date format is YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS. If MM/DD/YYYY or Day-Month is entered, It will be converted into the correct date and time format

Indicates whether an Operation Sequence in a Work Order header must be explicitly reported on or not when being moved to a Status of Complete. An Operation Sequence must be set as having a Count Point or be Automatically Transacted. Valid value is Y or N. During CREATE, you can optional define the Flag. If set = Y, then you do not set the Automatically Transact flag. If set = N, then you must set the Automatically Transaction Flag = Y. If set = null, then the default value is set = Y. It is reco

Indicates that the Operation Sequence in a Work Order header will be automatically reported during Work Order Execution. An Operation Sequence must be set as having a Count Point or be Automatically Transacted. Valid value is Y or N. During CREATE, you can optional define the Flag, based on the Count Point Flag. If set = Y, then the Count Point Flag must be set = N. If set = N, then the Count Point Flag must be set = Y. If set = null, then the default value is set = N. During UPDATE, you can upd

Indicates that the Operation Sequence in a Work Order header can be Edited and resequenced during work execution. Only Count Point operations can be defined as resequenceable operations, as long as they are not the first or last Operation Sequence in a Work Order header. Valid value is Y or N. During CREATE, you can optional define the Flag. If set = null, then the default value is set = N. During UPDATE, you can update the Flag until the Work Order is Released, else set = null and the flag is i

Value that uniquely identifies the outside processing (OSP) item representing the service expected from the supplier. During CREATE, if the Operation Type = Supplier, then an Item is required. Else, set = Null. During UPDATE, you can update the Item until the Work Order is Released, else set = null.

Name of the supplier performing the outside processing operation. The value will be used to create the purchase requisition. During CREATE, if the Operation Type = Supplier, then a Supplier Name is optional. If defined, then a Supplier Site is also required. Else, set = null. Note: if the previous Operation Sequence in a Work Order is of Type = Supplier, then the Supplier Name and Site are required. During UPDATE, you can update the Supplier until the Work Order is Released, else set = null.

Supplier Site where the outside processing operation will be executed. It is dependent on the Supplier Name value. During CREATE, if the Operation Type = Supplier and a Supplier Name is defined, then the Site is required. Else, set = null. Note: if the previous Operation Sequence in a Work Order is of Type = Supplier, then the Supplier Name and Site are required. During UPDATE, you can update the Supplier Site, for a Supplier Name, until the Work Order is Released, else set = null.

Indicates that the shipment needs to be created in order to print the shipping documents for the outside processing item. Valid values are Y or N. During CREATE, the value is optional. If set = null, then the default value is based on the Outside Processing Item's shippable attribute. During UPDATE, you can update the Flag until the Work Order is Released, else set = null.

Value that indicates a fixed lead time necessary to perform the supplier operation outside processing (OSP) item quantity. During CREATE, the value is optional, else set = null. During UPDATE, you can update the value until the Work Order is Released, else set = null.

Value that indicates the lead time necessary to perform the supplier operation for each unit of the outside processing (OSP) item. During CREATE, the value is optional, else set = null. During UPDATE, you can update the value until the Work Order is Released, else set = null.

Abbreviation that uniquely identifies the operation quantity unit of measure (UOM) to perform the supplier operation. During CREATE, the value is optional, else set = null. During UPDATE, you can update the value until the Work Order is Released, else set = null.

Abbreviation that optionally identifies the Reason for Repair for the Maintenance Work Order Operation. Valid values are defined as Condition Event Codes using the Type of Reason for repair code. During CREATE, if a Work Definition is not defined using a Referenced Standard Operation, then this attribute can be defined, else set = Null. During UPDATE the Code can be updated, else set = Null.

Abbreviation that optionally identifies the Primary Reason for Repair for the Maintenance Work Order Operation. Valid values are defined as Condition Event Codes using the Type of Transaction code. During CREATE, if a Work Definition is not defined using a Referenced Standard Operation, then this attribute can be defined, else set = Null. During UPDATE the Code can be updated, else set = Null.

Abbreviation that optionally identifies the Primary Reason for Repair for the Maintenance Work Order Operation. Valid values are defined as Condition Event Codes using the Type of Work accomplished code. During CREATE, if a Work Definition is not defined using a Referenced Standard Operation, then this attribute can be defined, else set = Null. During UPDATE the Code can be updated, else set = Null.

Abbreviation that identifies the unique Resource assigned to the Resource Sequence in the Operation Sequence of a Work Order. During CREATE, a Resource Code is required. Dring UPDATE, a Resource Code can't be updated and will be ignored, set = null.

The Resource usage rate required to repair the work order quantity. During CREATE, either Usage Rate or Required Usage is required to create an operation resource. For a Maintenance Work Order, these will be typically the same value as the maintenance the work order quantity is typically a value of 1 During UPDATE, the value can be updated.

A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type EGP_BOM_BASIS_TYPE. FIXED: the resource consumption is fixed. It does not change according to work order quantity. VARIABLE: the resource consumption is not fixed. It might change according to work order quantity. During CREATE, if a value is not passed, then the default value is VARIABLE. The required Resource usage for the repair of the work order quantity. This values depends on whether the basis type is FIXED or VARIABLE. Fixed: the required usage equals the usage rate. Variable: the required usage is the product of the usage rate and the work order quantity. During CREATE, either Usage Rate or Required Usage is required to create an operation resource. During UPDATE, the value can be updated.

Indicates if the Resource will be scheduled or not. Contains one of the following values: Y or N. Valid values are from lookup ORA_WIS_RESOURCE_SCHEDULE During CREATE or UPDATE, if the Flag is set = Y, then the resource is Scheduled and receives updated Scheduled Start Date and Completion Dates. If the Flag is set = N, then the resources is NOT Scheduled and its Scheduled Start Date and Completion Dates are set to the Operation Completion Dates. If set = Null, then a value of Y is passed.

Abbreviation that identifies how the resource is charged. Valid values include MANUAL or AUTOMATIC. A list of accepted values is defined in the lookup type ORA_WIS_CHARGE_TYPE. During CREATE, the charge type is required. For a Count Point Operation, this value can be MANUAL or AUTOMATIC. For an Automatically Transacted Operation, this value must be AUTOMATIC. For an optional Operation, this value must be MANUAL. For UPDATE, the same validations apply, else set = Null if not updating.

Abbreviation for the Job Profile that contains all the skills and qualifications required by a Labor Resource. Valid values are pre-defined using the Profile Code for an active Job Profile in Human resource employee profile. When it’s specified for a labor resource, then only those resource instances that meet the qualifications can be reported for resource transactions. During CREATE, the Type is optional, else set = Null. During UPDATE, the value can be updated, else set = Null.

Abbreviation for the Equipment Profile all the skills and qualifications required by an Equipment Resource. Valid values come from a pre-defined Profile Code for Equipment qualifications. When it’s specified for an equipment resource, then only those resource instances that meet the qualifications can be reported for resource transactions. During CREATE, the Type is optional, else set = Null. During UPDATE, the value can be updated, else set = Null.

The receiprocal value of the resource usage rate. This attribute is applicable when the resource Usage Rate is fractional but its inverse is an integer. During CREATE or UPDATE, the Value is optional. if a Usage Rate is not provided then the same is calculated from the Inverse Value. If both are provided then the Usage Rate value takes the precedence.
The number of resourceses working concurrently on this operation. During CREATE and UPDATE this value is optional. If not defined, then the the default value is 1.

Indicator that a resource is the principal resource within a group of simultaneous resources. Contains one of the following values: true or false During CREATE, if the Flag is set = Y, then this resource is the principal resource among the group of simultaneous resources. If the Flag = N, then this resource is not the principal resource. If set = Null, then the Flag is set = N. Note that one of the simultaneous resources must be a principal resource.

Abbreviation that describes the type of activity the resource will be performing in the operation. Valid seeded values are: ORA_RUN ORA_SETUP ORA_TEAR_DOWN Complete list of values are from lookup ORA_WIS_RESOURCE_ACTIVITY During CREATE and UPDATE, the Activity Code is optional.

Abbreviation that optionally identifies the Reason for Repair for the Maintenance Work Order Operation Resource. Valid values are defined as Condition Event Codes using the Type of Reason for repair code. During CREATE, if a Work Definition is not defined using a Referenced Standard Operation, then this attribute can be defined, else set = Null. During UPDATE the Code can be updated, else set = Null.

Abbreviation that optionally identifies the Primary Reason for Repair for the Maintenance Work Order Operation Resource. Valid values are defined as Condition Event Codes using the Type of Transaction code. During CREATE, if a Work Definition is not defined using a Referenced Standard Operation, then this attribute can be defined, else set = Null. During UPDATE the Code can be updated, else set = Null.

Abbreviation that optionally identifies the Primary Reason for Repair for the Maintenance Work Order Operation Resource. Valid values are defined as Condition Event Codes using the Type of Work accomplished code. During CREATE, if a Work Definition is not defined using a Referenced Standard Operation, then this attribute can be defined, else set = Null. During UPDATE the Code can be updated, else set = Null.
